reviewMethod: Fresh original-resolution inspection of all six formal stills and both formal contact sheets; complete formal 48-frame clips are byte-identical to the two previously inspected complete clips

answers.reason: Both formal sequences show continuous gravity-, inertia-, collision- and support-driven motion without a jump or glide into the result.
Sphere-to-shutter and basketball-to-bottle contacts remain continuous; adjacent formal frames resolve the crowded D1 edge without deep penetration.
The shutter and bottles begin responding only after visible contact and the mechanical cause remains legible.
The gate overshoots and settles, while the bottles respond and settle asymmetrically rather than moving as synchronized poses.
Wide, contact and effect views expose approach, collision and consequence in both formal sequences.
Measured native blur communicates speed while preserving seams, silhouettes and contact direction.
D1 warm illumination expands only as solved shutter geometry clears the static source aperture.
All three formal H1 bottles respond through contact; two remain down and one returns upright under the solver.
Sphere/basketball detail, bottle shoulders/caps/labels, gate ribs, rails and receiver remain recognizable at action distance.
Both formal end states are supported by the floor, hinge and preceding simulated paths rather than arranged for the camera.

fileDifferenceInterpretation: Formal still PNGs and the H1 contact-sheet PNG have render-sampling byte differences, but direct inspection finds no changed action, contact, framing or verdict. Both complete formal MP4 files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed complete clips.
limitations: The solver-owned action is accepted, but asset and environment realism remain below finished-film quality.
The current model does not simulate liquid slosh, deformation, debris or sound.
The D1 contact insert remains crowded enough that the complete sequence is more trustworthy than the isolated contact still.
